subject: Clarify VRAM-hour commit & SLA redline for Dedicated pool

Cc: sara.vance@heliotrope.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit definitions — follow-up questions

Hi Dev,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra and procurement teams reviewed the Dedicated Capacity brief and have two items they need clarified before procurement can move forward:

1) Capacity unit definition — your proposal ties commits to "capacity units" but our finance team needs a mapping to something we can forecast against (vRAM-hours, or equivalent GPU-hour). Can you provide a deterministic conversion for the M60/NVIDIA A100/L4 model families you quoted?

2) SLA/remedy quantification — we need the service-credit schedule in terms of percent monthly credit for specific latency/availability breaches. The draft T&Cs you sent are high level. Can you attach a concrete schedule and an example calculation?

We'd like to keep the commercial term but need these clarified in writing. Sara (cc) will be coordinating the legal review.

Best,
Oliver
Procurement Manager
Heliotrope Biomed

Attachments: none

Subject: Re: Dedicated commit definitions — follow-up questions

Hi Oliver / Sara,

Appreciate the thoughtful questions. High level answers below; attaching a short matrix and a proposed redline for the contract. See attachments: "Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Redline_v3.pdf" and "SLA_ServiceCredit_Schedule.xlsx".

1) Capacity units -> vRAM-hours:
- We define a capacity unit as 1,000 vRAM-hours at a 1.0 throughput baseline (this baseline equals ~1 full A100-80GB GPU for 1 hour).
- Conversion factors are in the attached PDF; for quick reference: A100-80GB = 1.0 cu per 1,000 vRAM-hours, A100-40GB = 0.55 cu, L4 = 0.12 cu (approx). These are conservative and tied to median token throughput from our benchmark suite (sequence length 512).

2) SLA/service credits:
- The attached spreadsheet maps availability tiers and median-95 latency guarantees to monthly credit percentages and example calculations. Example: if monthly availability falls to 98.5% (SLO 99.9%), the credit is 10% of monthly Dedicated fee for that customer. Larger breaches scale up to 60% for multi-week total outage.

Notes on throughput guarantees: we can guarantee sustained token-per-second throughput per reserved vRAM tranche rather than per GPU instance; that allows more stable economics when customers mix model families. The redline suggests language to express throughput as "sustained tokens/sec per 1,000 vRAM-hours" and an explicit fallbacks section if underlying hardware is changed.

I'll flag the items that are typically negotiated: conversion factors, minimum commit term for a discounted price band, and remedies caps. Happy to hop on a quick call Monday to walk the matrix.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Head of Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated commit definitions — follow-up questions

Sara / Oliver — quick internal note from my side and a proposed compromise on remedy caps.

1) Measurement windows: We propose ISO calendar-month windows with 5-minute sampling for availability and per-minute sampling for latency. We can include explicit computation pseudocode in the SOW annex. That keeps things auditable.

2) Force majeure: Redwood can accept cloud-provider maintenance as force majeure only if Redwood provides proof of provider maintenance that affected the capacity. For platform-level orchestration faults (e.g., routing/config errors) Redwood will not claim force majeure.

3) Remedy caps: Instead of a flat monetary cap, propose a sliding cap tied to committed vRAM-hours:
- 12-mo commit: cap = 100% of 1 month of committed fees
- 24-mo commit: cap = 150% of 1 month of committed fees
- 36-mo commit: cap = 200% of 1 month of committed fees

This aligns incentives — larger commit length raises the cap proportionally. We're not proposing uncapped liability, but want a commercial tiering that matches commit term.

On the runbook and named SE: we can commit to a named escalation engineer for 90 days and provide a 24/7 incident page during the onboarding window.

I can draft precise wording in the redline; Dev / Rishi — anything to add on conversion fairness or throughput expression?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of GTM Contracts
Redwood Inference

Sara — quick technical confirmation from infra side to support the contract language.

- The vRAM-hour mapping in the redline is conservative and based on median sustained throughput for sequence length distributions you've given (typical pipeline: 128-512 tokens per request). We will include a CSV benchmark annex showing measured tokens/sec per GPU class and how we derived the conversion factors.

- Throughput guarantees: we can guarantee sustained tokens/sec per 1,000 vRAM-hours as Dev suggested, but need to limit bursty short-term spikes. Proposed clause: "Sustained throughput guarantees are measured over a rolling 5-minute window; short-term bursts are outside this guarantee and may be throttled to preserve pool fairness."

- Fallback models: if a specific GPU family is unavailable, Redwood will provide a functionally equivalent model variant and compensate the customer via either (a) proportional credit or (b) temporary uplift in vRAM-hours for parity. The chosen remedy will be negotiable but documented as options in the SOW.

If this aligns with your expectations I'll put the benchmark annex into the redline and export a PDF for your review.

-Rishi
Director, Infra & Reliability
Redwood Inference
